papers.title: Persistent atrial fibrillation in older adults: Comparison of seven models and development of a gradient boosting machine classifier in a single-center observational study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate clinical correlates of persistent atrial fibrillation (AF) in older adults, compare seven classification models, and interpret the selected gradient boosting machine (GBM) classifier. This single-center observational study included 572 adults reported to be aged ≥ 60 years who received care between June 2021 and June 2023, comprising 385 participants classified as having persistent AF and 187 comparators. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) were used for candidate-variable assessment and f
papers.summary: This single-center observational study of 572 older adults compared seven classification models for identifying persistent atrial fibrillation and selected a gradient boosting machine classifier as the best performer. The work also characterizes clinical correlates of persistent AF in this population and interprets the chosen model's predictors.

papers.title: Machine-learning-assisted multi-omics profiling identifies CALB1 as a subtype-associated regulator of PI3K/AKT signaling and malignant progression in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is molecularly heterogeneous, and computationally nominated biomarkers often lack sufficient functional validation. CALB1 is a calcium-binding protein, but its clinical relevance, cellular source, and signaling role in NSCLC remain unclear. This study aimed to identify subtype-associated regulators in NSCLC through a machine-learning-assisted multi-omics framework and to characterize the functional and signaling relevance of CALB1 in malignant progression.
papers.summary: This study used a machine-learning-assisted multi-omics framework to identify subtype-associated regulators in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), nominating CALB1, a calcium-binding protein, as a candidate. The authors then functionally characterized CALB1, linking it to PI3K/AKT signaling and malignant progression, thereby providing validation for a computationally nominated biomarker.

papers.title: A survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and its prognostic relevance in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked clinical and immunological heterogeneity, and conventional clinicopathological variables do not fully capture patient survival risk. CD8+ T cells play a central role in antitumor immunity, yet their functional states can encompass both effective cytotoxic responses and dysfunctional immune programs. This study aimed to derive a survival-informed CD8+ T cell-associated gene signature and evaluate its prognostic associations, cellular expression, and relationship to immune dysfunction.
papers.summary: The study derives a gene signature associated with CD8+ T cells that is informed by survival outcomes in clear cell renal cell carcinoma, aiming to capture the dual cytotoxic and dysfunctional states of these immune cells. It evaluates the signature's prognostic value and its relationship to immune dysfunction, addressing the limitations of conventional clinicopathological variables in predicting patient risk.

papers.title: Development and validation of a phase-stable computed tomography radiomics model for brain metastasis risk stratification in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Brain metastasis (BM) is a frequent complication of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but individualized risk stratification remains limited. We evaluated whether computed tomography (CT) radiomic features reproducible across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced phases could improve BM risk prediction and whether integration with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings provided additional value.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates a CT radiomics model using features that remain stable across non-enhanced and contrast-enhanced imaging phases to stratify brain metastasis risk in non-small cell lung cancer patients. The authors also test whether combining radiomic features with clinical biomarkers and semantic CT findings improves predictive performance over radiomics alone.

papers.title: Multi-omics and pathological landscape of a senescence-associated prognostic model in bladder urothelial carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Cellular senescence contributes to tumor progression and shapes the tumor microenvironment (TME), yet its prognostic and biological significance in bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify senescence-associated prognostic signals through pan-cancer screening and to develop an integrated risk stratification framework for BLCA that bridges molecular characterization with translational relevance.
papers.summary: The authors built a senescence-associated prognostic model for bladder urothelial carcinoma by screening pan-cancer senescence signals and integrating multi-omics and pathological data. The model stratifies patients by risk and links senescence signatures to tumor microenvironment features, aiming to connect molecular characterization with clinical translation.

papers.title: From risk factors to individualized prediction: development and internal validation of a machine learning model for early identification of postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery.
papers.abstract: Postoperative pneumonia (POP) remains one of the most common infectious complications following lung cancer surgery and is associated with substantial morbidity. Although several risk factors for POP have been identified, clinically applicable approaches for early individualized risk stratification remain limited. This study aimed to develop and internally validate machine learning models for early prediction of POP using routinely available perioperative variables.
papers.summary: This study develops and internally validates machine learning models to predict postoperative pneumonia after lung cancer surgery using routinely collected perioperative variables. The goal is to enable earlier, individualized risk stratification beyond traditional risk-factor identification. As an internal validation study, the model's generalizability to other hospitals remains to be established.

papers.title: Building from the ground up: augmentation strategies to improve protein language model performance on protein sets.
papers.abstract: An important underlying requirement for deep learning models is the availability of large datasets, however, in sciences such as chemistry and biology, generating experimental data of sufficient size represents a significant bottleneck. In this work, we probed the extent and nature of limited input data, characterize how several protein language models (pLMs) learned on suboptimal datasets, and investigated augmentation approaches to improve predictive model performance. We found that narrowing the distribution of protein-protein complexes in a limited dataset permits an order-ofmagnitude decr
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates how protein language models (pLMs) perform when trained on small, limited datasets, a common bottleneck in biology. The authors characterize how dataset size and distribution affect pLM learning and test data augmentation strategies to improve predictive performance. They find that narrowing the distribution of protein-protein complexes in a limited dataset allows for an order-of-magnitude reduction in data requirements.

papers.title: AI-based prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in node-positive, HR+ breast cancer: a blinded external validation on SWOG-8814 trial.
papers.abstract: The benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy varies among patients with postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Genomic assays identify patients likely to benefit from chemotherapy but are expensive and tissue consuming. AI-enabled biomarkers may provide scalable alternatives. We performed a blinded external evaluation of Ataraxis Breast CTX, a causal multi-modal AI model that integrates H&E images with clinical variables, in the phase III SWOG-8814 trial.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This study externally validated an AI model, Ataraxis Breast CTX, that combines H&E histology images with clinical data to predict prognosis and chemotherapy benefit in postmenopausal, node-positive, hormone receptor-positive breast cancer. Using a blinded evaluation on the SWOG-8814 phase III trial, the authors assessed whether this scalable, tissue-sparing AI biomarker could serve as an alternative to expensive genomic assays for guiding adjuvant chemotherapy decisions.

papers.title: Functional architecture of rare protein coding variation across 786,871 exomes.
papers.abstract: Protein coding variants span the gamut of structural and functional effects on proteins, and they have similarly heterogeneous effects on traits. Their functional effects can be predicted and categorized, particularly using machine learning models, and integrating these predictors benefits gene discovery. However, it remains unclear how well known structural features and predicted functional scores explain the heterogeneous effects of protein coding variants on human complex traits. We introduce the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), which integrates multiple functional annotations to form a
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: This preprint introduces the Kernel Allelic Series Model (KASM), a method that combines multiple functional annotations and machine learning-based predictors to model how rare protein-coding variants affect complex traits. Applied across 786,871 exomes, it shows that integrating structural features and predicted functional scores improves gene discovery and explains heterogeneous variant effects better than single-annotation approaches.

papers.title: Predicting cell-state-specific gene regulation from DNA across species.
papers.abstract: DNA encodes the cell's phenotype, but the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently in every cell type, developmental stage, and activity state. Existing deep-learning models solve only half of this puzzle: sequence-to-function models read DNA but treat cell state as a fixed label, while single-cell foundation models represent cell state but not sequence. We developed Bolero, a sequence-to-function model whose parameters condition on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings and additional biological variables to predict cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance from DNA.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Bolero is a deep-learning model that predicts how the same DNA sequence is interpreted differently across cell types and states by conditioning sequence-to-function predictions on atlas-scale cell-state embeddings. It bridges the gap between sequence-based models that ignore cell state and single-cell foundation models that ignore DNA sequence, predicting cell-state-specific chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance directly from DNA.

papers.title: De novo Design of a Vanadium Haloperoxidase.
papers.abstract: Organohalogens are an essential class of compounds for both synthetic chemistry and natural systems, yet the design of halogenases to catalyze carbon-halogen (C-X) bond formation has remained elusive. Vanadium-dependent haloperoxidases (V-HPOs) are attractive targets for such an effort, but they pose an unusual design problem: the vanadate (VO 4 3- ) cofactor is an anionic oxometalate that must be held by a precisely arranged network of hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions rather than by the strong coordinate-covalent bonds through which proteins bind cationic transition metals. We
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint reports the de novo design of a vanadium-dependent haloperoxidase, an enzyme that catalyzes carbon-halogen bond formation using a vanadate cofactor. The key challenge is that vanadate is an anionic oxometalate requiring precise hydrogen-bonding and electrostatic interactions rather than the coordinate-covalent bonds typical for metal-binding proteins. The work demonstrates that computational protein design can create a functional halogenase, a class of enzymes previously difficult to engineer.

papers.title: Distance-AF Multimer: A Multi-Step Approach for Protein Complex Structure Modeling with User-Defined Distance Constraints.
papers.abstract: The three-dimensional structure of proteins provides essential insight into the molecular mechanisms underlying their function. Many biological activities are mediated through protein interactions, making accurate structural determination of protein complexes important. Despite significant advances in computational protein structure prediction, there are still many cases where protein complexes are not correctly assembled. In particular, there are cases where experimental data, such as distances between residue pairs in interacting proteins are available, yet existing prediction methods fail t
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Distance-AF Multimer is a new computational pipeline that incorporates user-defined distance constraints into AlphaFold-Multimer to improve protein complex structure prediction. It addresses cases where experimental distance data (e.g., crosslinks) are available but standard methods fail to assemble complexes correctly. The approach provides a multi-step workflow for integrating these constraints, likely improving accuracy in challenging modeling scenarios.

papers.title: Multimodal Integration Identifies C16orf74 as an EMT Regulator With Prognostic Relevance in HNSCC.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by marked intratumoral heterogeneity and poor clinical outcomes. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) promotes metastasis, immune evasion, and therapeutic resistance. However, the key molecular determinants underlying EMT-associated malignant states remain incompletely defined, and their translation into clinically accessible tools is challenging. In this study, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in HNSCC. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) i
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk multi-omics data to dissect malignant epithelial heterogeneity in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, identifying C16orf74 as a novel regulator of epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT). The authors show that C16orf74 expression is associated with EMT-associated malignant states and has prognostic relevance in HNSCC patients.

papers.title: Estimating rates of SARS-CoV-2 lineage spread using graph spectra from genetic sequence data.
papers.abstract: The modern enormous scale of viral genomic data, as exemplified by SARS-CoV-2, presents unique opportunities for epidemic inference and real-time monitoring. A key challenge is to wade through the extremely large stream of sequence data in order to identify small subsets of sequences that may represent rapid population growth of newly emerged lineages. To address this challenge, we developed a new approach that combines techniques in graph theory and machine learning. We represent distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians and identify from them features of rapid populati
papers.summary: The authors present a new method that combines graph theory and machine learning to estimate the rate of spread of SARS-CoV-2 lineages from genetic sequence data. By representing distances between small subsets of sequences as graph Laplacians, they extract features that identify lineages undergoing rapid population growth. This enables real-time monitoring of large viral genomic datasets to flag emerging lineages of concern.

papers.title: EZpred: Improving Deep Learning-Based Enzyme Function Prediction Using Unlabeled Sequence Homologs.
papers.abstract: Features extracted from sequence homologs significantly enhance the accuracy of deep learning-based protein structure prediction. Indeed, homolog-aware models such as AlphaFold generally produce more accurate protein structures compared to single sequence-based methods like ESMfold. In contrast, features from sequence homologs are seldom employed for deep learning-based prediction of the biological functions of a protein, such as Gene Ontology terms or Enzyme Commission (EC) numbers. Although a small number of models also incorporate function labels from sequence homologs, they cannot utilize
papers.summary: EZpred is a deep learning method that improves enzyme function prediction (EC number assignment) by incorporating features from unlabeled sequence homologs, analogous to how AlphaFold leverages homologous sequences for structure prediction. This addresses a gap where most function-prediction models ignore the rich evolutionary signal available in unlabeled homologs. The approach likely boosts accuracy by exploiting conserved patterns across related sequences without requiring labeled data for those homologs.

papers.title: Preoperative discrimination of malignant and benign ovarian masses using cfDNA fragmentomics and serum biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Preoperative discrimination of ovarian cancer from benign masses poses significant challenges, particularly in cases where serum biomarkers yield negative or nonspecific results. This multicenter observational diagnostic modeling study analyzed plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) from 743 participants across training, internal test, external test, and two exploratory cohorts using low-pass whole-genome sequencing. Four fragmentomic feature classes-fragment size patterns, nucleosome footprint-related features, copy-number variations, and repeat element patterns-were incorporated into a stacked machine
papers.summary: This multicenter study developed a diagnostic model combining cfDNA fragmentomic features (fragment size, nucleosome footprints, copy-number variations, repeat element patterns) from low-pass whole-genome sequencing with serum biomarkers to distinguish malignant from benign ovarian masses. The stacked machine-learning model was trained and validated across 743 participants in multiple cohorts, addressing the clinical problem of indeterminate or negative serum biomarker results preoperatively.

papers.title: Bacterial protein function prediction via multimodal deep learning.
papers.abstract: Bacterial proteins are specialized with extensive functional diversity for survival in diverse and stressful environments. A significant portion of these proteins remains functionally uncharacterized, limiting our understanding of bacterial survival mechanisms. Hence, we develop Deep Expression STructure (DeepEST), a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts protein function in bacteria by assigning Gene Ontology (GO) terms. DeepEST comprises two modules: a multi-layer perceptron that uses gene expression and gene location, and a protein structure-based module that uses predicted struct
papers.summary: The authors developed DeepEST, a multimodal deep learning framework that predicts Gene Ontology terms for bacterial proteins by combining gene expression, gene location, and predicted protein structure. This approach addresses the large fraction of bacterial proteins that remain functionally uncharacterized, potentially improving annotation in diverse and stressful environments.

papers.title: Explainable AI identifies recombination and chromatin environment as key predictors of subgenome evolution in maize and Brassica.
papers.abstract: Polyploidy, or whole genome duplication, reshapes genomes through biased gene loss and regulatory rewiring, yet the drivers of biased fractionation among subgenomes remain unclear. Using maize and Brassica rapa as model allopolyploids, we compiled 60 genomic and epigenomic features in maize and 45 in B. rapa and constructed supervised machine learning models to classify genes by subgenome identity. In both species, eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) approaches identified recombination rate as the most influential and highly interconnected feature despite nonsignificant mean differences
papers.summary: This study used supervised machine learning and explainable AI to identify which genomic and epigenomic features best predict subgenome identity in two allopolyploids, maize and Brassica rapa. Across 60 features in maize and 45 in B. rapa, recombination rate emerged as the most influential and highly interconnected predictor, along with chromatin environment, despite showing no significant mean differences between subgenomes. The work suggests biased fractionation after whole-genome duplication is driven by recombination and chromatin context rather than simple feature-level differences.

papers.title: Development and Validation of Machine Learning Models Incorporating TGFBIp Expression for Prognosis Prediction in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer.
papers.abstract: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) exhibits substantial heterogeneity in clinical outcomes, highlighting the need for diverse prognostic tools. Transforming growth factor-β-induced protein (TGFBIp) has been implicated in ovarian cancer progression, but its incremental prognostic value within machine learning frameworks remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study develops and validates machine learning prognostic models for epithelial ovarian cancer that incorporate TGFBIp expression alongside other clinical and molecular features. The authors aim to show that adding TGFBIp improves outcome prediction over existing tools, addressing the heterogeneity of EOC prognosis.

papers.title: Metabolic Profiling Combined With Machine Learning for Assessing Clonal Hematopoiesis Status in Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenia: An Exploratory Analysis.
papers.abstract: Clonal hematopoiesis (CH) has emerged as a potential contributor to the pathogenesis of immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), yet the clinical and metabolic features of ITP patients harboring CH-associated mutations remain poorly characterized. We retrospectively analyzed a genomic discovery cohort of 1817 patients with chronic ITP, identifying CH in 196 individuals (10.8%), with DNMT3A as the most frequently mutated gene. In a metabolomic profiling cohort of 539 patients (492 ITP-non-CH, 47 ITP-CH), we characterized plasma metabolic signatures using untargeted LC-MS/MS and systematically evaluated t
papers.summary: This exploratory study analyzed genomic data from 1,817 chronic ITP patients and found clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in 10.8%, most commonly involving DNMT3A. Using untargeted plasma metabolomics in a subset of 539 patients, the authors characterized metabolic signatures distinguishing ITP patients with CH from those without, and applied machine learning to assess CH status. The work suggests that metabolic profiling combined with ML could offer a non-genomic route to flag CH in ITP, though validation is needed.

papers.title: A machine learning-based predictive tool for complete renal response in lupus nephritis leverages the 3-month treatment milestone.
papers.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) remains a major determinant of poor prognosis in systemic lupus erythematosus, yet reliable tools for early identification of unfavorable renal outcomes are lacking. This study aimed to identify early prognostic factors for complete renal response (CRR) at 12 months in active LN and to develop interpretable machine learning (ML) models for early prediction of treatment response. In this prospective cohort of 400 active LN patients followed for 12 months, the primary outcome was 12-month CRR. Candidate predictors were assessed at baseline and 3-month follow-up. Four ML mode
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 400 active lupus nephritis patients used machine learning models to predict complete renal response at 12 months, with predictors assessed at baseline and at the 3-month treatment milestone. The key finding is that incorporating 3-month follow-up data improves early identification of patients likely to achieve complete renal response, enabling interpretable risk stratification.

papers.title: Predicting the alternative conformation of a known protein structure based on the distogram of AlphaFold2.
papers.abstract: AlphaFold2 (AF2) has become one of the most established and leading tools for predicting protein structures, although it often favors a single conformation. While it has been shown that sampling different conformations is possible by manipulating the multiple sequence alignment (MSA), the potential for multi-state information within a standard AF2 prediction remains underexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that even with a deep MSA, AF2 predictions encode structural heterogeneity. Specifically, we observe that the predicted residue-residue distance distributions often exhibit multiple proba
papers.summary: This study shows that AlphaFold2's predicted residue-residue distance distributions (distograms) contain information about multiple protein conformations, even when the model outputs a single structure from a deep multiple sequence alignment. By analyzing these distributions, the authors demonstrate that alternative conformational states can be predicted from a standard AF2 prediction, offering a way to extract multi-state structural information without manipulating the MSA.

papers.title: Development of a Machine-Learning Model for Strongyloidiasis Risk Stratification in Migrant Populations.
papers.abstract: Strongyloidiasis is a parasitic infection with the potential for fatal hyperinfection, underscoring the need for screening strategies. A machine-learning model was developed and externally validated to support strongyloidiasis risk stratification among migrants from endemic areas.
papers.journal: Research and reports in tropical medicine
papers.summary: This study developed and externally validated a machine-learning model to stratify strongyloidiasis risk among migrants from endemic areas, addressing the need for targeted screening given the potential for fatal hyperinfection. The model aims to support clinical decision-making by identifying high-risk individuals for screening.

papers.title: A lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for Kazakh Sign Language recognition under signer-independent conditions.
papers.abstract: Sign Language Recognition (SLR) in low-resource sign languages is still limited due to the lack of annotated data, high variability of signers, and lack of benchmarks; Kazakh Sign Language (KzSL) is a representative example of such a low-resource language. The proposed research introduces a novel method for isolated KzSL recognition based on a purpose-collected dataset of RGB video streams of five signers, represented by 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, facial, and hand landmark vectors extracted using MediaPipe Holistic. The final dataset consists of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 output c
papers.summary: The authors present a lightweight multi-branch transformer architecture for recognizing isolated Kazakh Sign Language gestures from RGB video, using MediaPipe Holistic to extract 1662-dimensional per-frame pose, face, and hand landmark vectors. They collected a new dataset of 39,979 gesture samples across 187 classes from five signers and evaluate under signer-independent conditions, addressing the low-resource SLR gap for KzSL. The work contributes both a dataset and a compact model tailored to signer variability.

papers.title: SelCysML: a hybrid ML-BLAST pipeline for the automated identification and functional annotation of bacterial selenoproteins.
papers.abstract: Selenoproteins are characterized by the incorporation of selenocysteine (Sec) via UGA codon recoding, play vital roles in redox homeostasis and enzymatic catalysis. Despite this biological significance, their computational identification remains challenging, and recent assessments confirm that public databases suffer from widespread annotation errors, often misclassifying these proteins. Current predictive tools frequently operate as "black boxes" with limited interpretability or lack integrated functional validation layers, which contributes to high false-positive rates and persistent ambigui
papers.summary: The authors present SelCysML, a hybrid pipeline that combines machine learning with BLAST homology searches to automatically identify bacterial selenoproteins and annotate their functions. The tool addresses the problem of widespread misannotation of selenoproteins in public databases, where UGA-recoding proteins are often incorrectly classified. By integrating interpretable ML with sequence-similarity validation, the pipeline aims to reduce false positives and improve functional assignment.

papers.title: Dietary amino acid composition and elevated fasting glucose in children and adolescents from four Chinese provinces: a cross-sectional study combining regression and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Using an integrated analytical pipeline that combines regression and machine learning, with nonlinear dose-response modeling, this cross-sectional study sought to examine dietary amino acid composition in relation to elevated fasting glucose (EFG) in children and adolescents.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examines whether the amino acid composition of children's diets is associated with elevated fasting glucose across four Chinese provinces. It combines traditional regression with machine learning and nonlinear dose-response modeling to identify dietary amino acid patterns linked to early glucose dysregulation. The work highlights a potential nutritional lever for pediatric metabolic risk, though causal inference is limited by the cross-sectional design.

papers.title: A reproducible open-data framework for interpretable breast cancer diagnosis and cytopathology education.
papers.abstract: Quantitative nuclear morphology links cytopathological assessment with interpretable diagnostic modeling and provides a practical foundation for teaching medical artificial intelligence. This study evaluated a reproducible framework that connects nuclear feature interpretation, malignant-versus-benign classification, and evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.
papers.summary: This study presents a reproducible open-data framework that uses quantitative nuclear morphology features to classify breast cytopathology as malignant or benign while keeping the diagnostic reasoning interpretable. The framework also serves as a teaching tool for medical AI, linking feature-level interpretation to evidence-based assessment of diagnostic decisions.

papers.title: Identifying potential targets in endothelial to mesenchymal transition-mediated atherosclerosis using bioinformatics and machine learning.
papers.abstract: Endothelial to mesenchymal transition (EndMT) is a key driver of atherosclerosis (AS). This study integrated multiple RNA transcriptomic and single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between EndMT and AS.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell RNA transcriptomic datasets to identify shared gene expression signatures between endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EndMT) and atherosclerosis. Using bioinformatics and machine learning, the authors pinpoint potential molecular targets linking EndMT to atherosclerotic disease. The work provides candidate genes for further experimental validation in cardiovascular disease.

papers.title: Development and temporal validation of an explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital diabetic foot ulcer in patients with type 2 diabetes using inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and temporally validate explainable machine learning models for predicting in-hospital new-onset DFU in hospitalized patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) using routinely available admission variables and inflammatory-nutritional composite indices.
papers.summary: This study develops and temporally validates explainable machine learning models to predict in-hospital new-onset diabetic foot ulcers in hospitalized type 2 diabetes patients, using routinely collected admission variables combined with inflammatory-nutritional composite indices. The work emphasizes model interpretability and temporal validation to support clinical risk stratification at admission.

papers.title: A deep learning model for automated assessment of neonates at risk of impaired breast crawl: a proof-of-concept video-based study.
papers.abstract: Timely initiation of breastfeeding is critical for newborn health. The breast crawl, an instinctive sequence of behaviors, is fundamental to this process. However, newborns vary considerably in their ability to complete the crawl, and current assessment relies on subjective endpoint observation. This approach cannot provide an early, objective measure of crawl competency or support timely intervention for at-risk mother-infant dyads.
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study proposes a deep learning model that analyzes videos of newborns to automatically assess their ability to perform the breast crawl, an instinctive behavior sequence important for breastfeeding initiation. The approach aims to replace subjective endpoint observation with an early, objective measure of crawl competency, potentially enabling timely intervention for at-risk mother-infant dyads.
